run.question: Our Elasticsearch cluster health is not green. Using the cluster tools, find out the cluster status, which index has unassigned shards and why the shard cannot be allocated, and check node resource usage. Report the cause.

report.summary: The Elasticsearch cluster named docker-cluster is yellow, not red: 4 of 5 shards are active (active_shards_percent_as_number 80.0), with exactly one unassigned shard and zero unassigned primaries. The single unassigned shard is the replica of cp1-orders shard 0: the cat shards view shows cp1-orders shard 0 as 'p' STARTED on node bea971fdc0c6 (172.17.0.2) and the 'r' copy of shard 0 as UNASSIGNED. The allocation explain API returns can_allocate 'no' for that shard and its only blocking decider is same_shard on node bea971fdc0c6 — 'a copy of this shard is already allocated to this node' — because the cluster has just one node (number_of_nodes 1, number_of_data_nodes 1) and only that one node is offered as an allocation candidate. The index cp1-orders is configured with number_of_shards 1, number_of_replicas 1; its unassigned_info records reason INDEX_CREATED at 2026-11-23T15:22:56.394Z with last_allocation_status no_attempt, i.e. the replica was never allocatable rather than lost after allocation. Node resources are not the blocking factor: the data path has 101,176,053,760 bytes available of 160,497,381,376 total (well above the reported low/high/flood watermarks), JVM heap is 1,236,042,720 of 2,147,483,648 bytes (57%), no breaker reports 'tripped', CPU percent is 4 and thread pools show zero queue and zero rejections. The consequence is index status yellow for cp1-orders only (the three system indices .ds-.logs-deprecation.elasticsearch-default-2026.11.23-000001, .ds-ilm-history-7-2026.11.23-000001 and .security-7 are green with 0 replicas); the cluster will stay yellow until either a second data node exists or the index's replica count is reduced to 0. All of this is the state at the moment of the query (observed_at 2026-11-23T15:23:07–15:23:10, inside the authorized window) and cannot prove the cluster's earlier state during the window.

claims.text: Cluster docker-cluster health is yellow: status 'yellow', unassigned_shards 1, unassigned_primary_shards 0, active_shards 4, active_shards_percent_as_number 80.0, number_of_nodes 1, number_of_data_nodes 1. Per-index health lists cp1-orders as yellow with number_of_shards 1, number_of_replicas 1, unassigned_shards 1, unassigned_primary_shards 0, while .ds-.logs-deprecation.elasticsearch-default-2026.11.23-000001, .ds-ilm-history-7-2026.11.23-000001 and .security-7 are green.

The unassigned shard belongs to index cp1-orders: cat shards for cp1-orders shows shard 0 role 'p' state STARTED on node bea971fdc0c6 (172.17.0.2) and shard 0 role 'r' state UNASSIGNED with null node. The index listing shows cp1-orders health yellow, status open, pri 1, rep 1, docs.count 0, store.size 227b.

Allocation explain for index cp1-orders shard 0 primary=false returns current_state 'unassigned', can_allocate 'no', allocate_explanation 'Elasticsearch isn't allowed to allocate this shard to any of the nodes in the cluster', and a single node_allocation_decision for node bea971fdc0c6 (yxF_y55zS0q2BKHN3zahxw) with node_decision 'no' whose only decider is same_shard: 'a copy of this shard is already allocated to this node [[cp1-orders][0], node[yxF_y55zS0q2BKHN3zahxw], [P], s[STARTED], a[id=hn2d80a0SjyoBzO8UKTagQ], failed_attempts[0]]'. No disk-watermark, allocation-filter or resource decider is listed as blocking.

The unassigned copy of cp1-orders shard 0 has unassigned_info at 2026-11-23T15:22:56.394Z with reason 'INDEX_CREATED' and last_allocation_status 'no_attempt', i.e. the replica was unassignable from index creation rather than lost after being allocated; the index currently holds docs.count 0.

Node resource usage is not exhausted: on node bea971fdc0c6 (/usr/share/elasticsearch/data, overlay mount) available_in_bytes 101176053760 of total_in_bytes 160497381376 with low_watermark_free_space_in_bytes 24074607206, high_watermark_free_space_in_bytes 16049738137 and flood_stage_free_space_in_bytes 8024869068; JVM heap_used_in_bytes 1236042720 of heap_max_in_bytes 2147483648 (heap_used_percent 57); breakers parent estimated_size_in_bytes 1236042720 under limit_size_in_bytes 2040109465 with tripped 0 on every breaker; os.cpu.percent 4; cat nodes reports cpu 5, heap.percent 57, load_1m 0.49; thread pools show queue 0 and rejected 0 (e.g. write completed 16, search completed 25); number_of_pending_tasks 0.

Node-level memory reporting is high on the host: os.mem.used_in_bytes 33091702784 of total_in_bytes 33648590848 (used_percent 98, free_percent 2), reported identically by cat nodes as ram.percent 98; JVM heap use itself is only 57%, and cgroup memory limit is 'max'.

Disk space/watermark pressure is not the reason the shard is unallocated: 101 GB of 160 GB is available on the data path, far above the low, high and flood-stage watermark free-space thresholds reported for that path, and the allocation explain output lists no disk decider — only same_shard — as the blocking decider on the sole candidate node.

JVM heap or breaker exhaustion is not the reason the shard is unallocated: heap is 57% used, no breaker reports tripped>0, thread-pool queues and rejections are 0 and there are 0 pending cluster tasks, and the explain API lists no memory/breaker decider blocking allocation.

The host-level memory reading (os.mem.used_percent 98, free 556,888,064 bytes of 33,648,590,848) is a separate capacity concern for node bea971fdc0c6 rather than the cause of the unassigned replica: allocation explain attributes the block solely to the same_shard decider, and JVM heap/breakers are healthy at the sampled moment. This would be confirmed by memory time series on the node and by observing whether allocation behaviour changes when host free memory rises.

To clear the yellow state, either add a second data node (so the cp1-orders replica can satisfy the same_shard constraint on a different node) or set cp1-orders number_of_replicas to 0 if a single-node cluster is intended; the explain API reports no other blocking decider, so no watermark or allocation-filter change is needed for this shard.

gaps: All Elasticsearch views are single-instant readings at observed_at 2026-11-23T15:23:07–15:23:10; they cannot show cluster health, shard allocation or node resource usage earlier in the authorized window (2026-10-24T15:23:05Z to 2026-11-23T15:23:05Z), so the duration and any previous state of the unassigned replica are unknown.

Whether the cluster ever had more than one data node, and when the cp1-orders index was created with number_of_replicas 1, cannot be established from these cluster state calls; the change_history integration is not available in this Run, so the index creation event's author and any prior settings change are unknown.

The first allocation-explain call without index/shard arguments explained a randomly chosen unassigned shard per its own note; the specific cp1-orders shard 0 replica was then explained explicitly and showed the same same_shard decider, but shards other than cp1-orders shard 0 were not individually explained (cluster health lists only this one unassigned shard).

No Elasticsearch-level impact beyond index health yellow is observed: no search/indexing errors, latency series or application logs from the cluster were queried in this Run, so client-visible consequences of the unassigned replica are unknown.
next_steps: Add a second data-role node to docker-cluster, or reduce cp1-orders number_of_replicas to 0, then re-check cluster health for green.
If index redundancy is required, keep number_of_replicas at 1 and instead grow the data-node count, since the same_shard decider can only be satisfied on a different node.
Monitor host memory on node bea971fdc0c6 (os.mem.used_percent 98) separately from JVM heap, since that is the only resource signal that looks elevated in this sample.
